[F3] says “The cell modules and simple modules are self-dual.” In characteristic 3, the (2,1) Specht module W={(x,y,z): x+y+z=0} for S3 has the trivial line k(1,1,1) and sign quotient, but no sign submodule: the simultaneous -1 eigenvector equations for (12) and (23) force zero. The item specifies no field F or invertible Hecke parameter q, yet calls ell=4 a characteristic. A field cannot have characteristic 4. Brundan defines ell as the field characteristic only when q=1; for q≠1 it is the order of q when q is a root of unity. The local branching dependencies cited here concern prime-characteristic group algebras, so they do not establish the ell=4 Hecke conclusions under the stated setup.

The paragraph says the example shows same-residue removable nodes can differ in normality and calls ell=3,4 characteristics. The ell=4 case is a quantum-characteristic case, not a field characteristic 4.
